skill.name: multi-agent-orchestration
skill.description: Orchestrate tasks across multiple AI providers (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, Ollama). Use when delegating tasks to specialized providers, routing based on capabilities, or implementing fallback strategies.
skill.summary: Route, delegate, and coordinate AI tasks across cloud and local providers.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives from Markdown, placeholders, localhost examples, and fixed commands. Gemini examples still submit local source to a cloud provider, and one example fetches an external domain. The Codex cookbook also recommends full auto-approval, creating a medium risk of unintended model actions.

remediation.issue: Gemini examples embed local file contents directly in cloud prompts.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user consent and a sensitive-data review before submission. Use an allowlist for every file sent to a cloud provider.

remediation.issue: The Codex cookbook recommends full auto-approval.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before full auto-approval. Document restrictive sandbox, filesystem, and network settings for every such invocation.

content.value_statement: Selecting the right AI provider for each task is difficult and costly. This skill routes work by capability, availability, privacy, and cost.
actual_capabilities: Routes tasks among Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, and Ollama using documented capability criteria.
Provides provider-specific setup, authentication, command, response, and error-handling guidance.
Defines fallback choices when a preferred provider is unavailable or unsuitable.
Coordinates parallel agents with roles, timeouts, result collection, and synthesis patterns.
Standardizes delegation results with provider, task, status, summary, and detail sections.
limitations: Required provider CLIs, accounts, API access, and local models must be installed and configured separately.
Referenced model discovery and orchestration scripts are not included in this skill package.
Provider capabilities, model names, pricing, and command flags can become outdated.
Cloud delegation can incur costs and transfer task data outside the local environment.

use_cases.title: Route Engineering Tasks
use_cases.description: Select a provider for code review, implementation, sandboxed tests, or large codebase analysis.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Parallel Research
use_cases.description: Assign distinct research roles, collect partial results, and synthesize findings within a defined timeout.

use_cases.title: Control AI Delivery Costs
use_cases.description: Match task complexity to provider and model tiers while retaining practical fallbacks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Provider
prompt_templates.prompt: Route this task to the best available provider: [task]. Explain the capability match, prerequisites, privacy impact, cost, and fallback before delegation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a single task with no preferred provider.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Delegation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a delegation plan for [project task]. Check provider availability and authentication. Keep conversation-dependent work in Claude Code.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before delegating a focused engineering task.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Parallel Agents
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a parallel workflow for [research goal]. Assign distinct roles, model tiers, timeouts, result collection, and synthesis. Limit agents to [number].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for research or analysis that benefits from independent perspectives.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Resilient Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an orchestration plan for [workflow]. Include consent checks, cost limits, provider fallbacks, partial failures, observability tags, and final synthesis.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced workflows spanning several providers.

output_examples.input: Review a small authentication change and run its tests in isolation.
output: Reason: The task needs sandboxed execution and focused code analysis.
Fallback: Claude for review without execution.

output_examples.input: Analyze a large repository and compare its architecture with current public guidance.
output: Reason: The task combines large context with web research.
Privacy note: Review repository files before cloud submission.

output_examples.input: Research three implementation approaches using four agents.
output: Four tagged workers receive distinct research questions.
Each worker has a three-minute timeout.
Completed results proceed to one synthesis step.
Failures are reported with reduced coverage confidence.

best_practices: Confirm provider availability, authentication, cost, and data-handling requirements before delegation.
Share only the minimum required context and obtain consent before sending sensitive data to cloud providers.
Use distinct agent roles, bounded timeouts, and explicit fallbacks for parallel work.
anti_patterns: Do not delegate tasks that depend on unavailable conversation history.
Do not use full auto-approval without explicit confirmation and restrictive sandbox settings.
Do not launch identical agents or expensive models when differentiated lower-cost workers are sufficient.

faq.question: Which providers does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor Agent, OpenCode, and local Ollama workflows.

faq.question: Does the skill install provider tools?
faq.answer: No. Install and authenticate each required CLI or local service separately.

faq.question: Can it keep sensitive data local?
faq.answer: It recommends Ollama for local processing. Confirm the service configuration and avoid cloud fallbacks for sensitive data.

faq.question: How does provider selection work?
faq.answer: The guidance compares task needs such as context size, sandboxing, web access, privacy, IDE integration, and cost.

faq.question: Does it support parallel agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents parallel launches, instance tags, timeouts, partial result handling, and synthesis.

faq.question: Are model names always current?
faq.answer: No. Use current provider documentation or the referenced model discovery tooling before selecting a model.
